draft.title: Pure substances and mixtures
card: a material made of only one kind of particle. An element has one type of atom. A compound has two or more elements joined chemically in a fixed ratio.
two or more substances that are not chemically joined. The amounts can vary, and each substance keeps its own properties.
Mixtures can be separated by physical means, which do not make new substances. Each method uses a difference in a property.

Filtration separates a solid from a liquid by particle size. Distillation separates liquids by boiling point. Chromatography separates substances by how far they travel through a material such as paper.
draft.remember: Mixtures separate by physical means that use a difference in properties.

a.q: Why is salt water a mixture and not a compound?
opts: Its salt and water are not joined chemically and can vary
Its salt and water are joined in one fixed ratio
It contains only one type of atom
It cannot be separated by physical means
a.why: Salt water has salt and water mixed together without being chemically joined, and the amount of salt can vary. A compound has a fixed ratio of elements joined chemically, so that option is wrong.
a.clue: Think about whether the amounts can change.

b.q: Ben has a mixture of ethanol and water, which are both liquids. The ethanol boils at a lower temperature than the water. Which method best separates them?
opts: Distillation
Filtration
Chromatography
Chemical reaction
b.why: Distillation uses the difference in boiling point to separate liquids. Filtration is tempting but only works when a solid is mixed with a liquid, because it relies on particle size.
b.clue: Which property differs between the two liquids?

a.best: Its salt and water are not joined chemically and can vary

problems.detail: Chromatography is said to separate substances 'by how far they travel through a material such as paper'. That is the result, not the property used. The card says each method uses a difference in a property, so it should name it: how strongly each substance is attracted to the paper compared with the solvent (or how soluble it is in the solvent).

The why says filtration 'only works when a solid is mixed with a liquid'. This is too strong: filtration separates an undissolved solid from a fluid, including a gas, as in air filters. It also fails for a solid dissolved in a liquid. Better: 'filtration separates an undissolved solid from a liquid by particle size, so it cannot separate two liquids.'

check.summary: Both questions are sound and have one clear answer: 'not joined chemically and can vary' for (a) and distillation for (b). There are two minor fixes: the card describes chromatography by its result rather than the property it uses, and the why for (b) overstates filtration with 'only'.
